solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Companion in apartment lifeless, getting Mike worried

parts.note: flat means dull or lifeless
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ate, as in 'what's eating you?', means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: Someone sharing a dull apartment frets about a man called Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' is not an anagram signal here: ATE is its past tense in the sense of gnawing at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatmate is the person you share a flat, the British word for an apartment, with.

clue.text: Old comedian's French knowledge

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: the Normans were French, from Normandy, so Norman can stand for French
wisdom is accumulated knowledge

explanation.surface: A veteran comic is said to have a good grasp of French.
explanation.walkthrough: Norman Wisdom was a British slapstick comedian of film and stage, popular from the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Wisdom is an example of a comedian from a past era, who died in 2010.

clue.text: Notice vicar rejected key part of speech

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for vicar is turned backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: A notice turned down by the vicar names a key grammatical element.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb is one of the word classes in grammar, modifying verbs and adjectives.

clue.text: Stagger back from park with painting

parts.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public park
an oil is a painting done in oils

explanation.surface: Someone reels away from a park scene on canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: REC is British slang for a recreation ground, a public playing field or park.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to start or flinch backwards in shock or disgust.

clue.text: Language used by neighbour dubious

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shady neighbour speaks a particular tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Old man cracked nut

indicators.note: cracked means broken apart, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elderly man has broken open a nut, or has gone mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is an edible kernel, a nut from the almond tree.

clue.text: English politician with passion for supreme dominion

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
ire is anger, a strong passion

explanation.surface: An English MP is passionate about having total power.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a realm under one supreme authority, a sovereign's dominion over many lands.

clue.text: Grill, with hesitation, US dough bread

parts.note: to grill and to pump both mean to question someone hard
er is the sound of hesitation
a nickel is a US five-cent coin; dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: A cook grills, pausing over American dough before baking bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' looks like a baking word but is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpernickel is a dense dark rye bread from Germany.

clue.text: Check stalk of plant

definitions.meaning: to ... a flow is to check or stop it
the main stalk of a plant

explanation.surface: Examine the stalk of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Stem as a verb means halt or restrain; as a noun it is a plant's stalk.

clue.text: Huge tailless rodent follows one around river

indicators.note: follows puts the rodent piece after the rest
around means turned round, so the word for one is read backwards

parts.note: taken as the word one

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter of the rodent is dropped

parts.note: a mouse is a small rodent

explanation.surface: A rodent without a tail trails someone round a river, enormous in scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a containment signal but here turns the word for one backwards; 'follows' puts the docked rodent last, and 'tailless' drops its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous and huge are synonyms, both meaning very large.

clue.text: Carthaginian leader beheaded man-eater on horse

indicators.note: on puts the trimmed man-eater after the horse piece

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a cannibal eats human flesh

explanation.surface: A headless man-eater rides a horse into battle as Carthage's general.
explanation.definitionFit: Hannibal was the general who led Carthage against Rome, crossing the Alps with elephants.

clue.text: Beer starts to affect lad excessively

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Beer is beginning to make a young man drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale is a type of beer, brewed with top-fermenting yeast.

clue.text: Two marks found in each novel

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency, so two of them give MM

explanation.surface: A pair of grades turns up in every novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's 1815 novel about a meddling matchmaker.

clue.text: Horse, near Aintree's front three, fell maybe

parts.note: a mount is a horse to ride

indicators.note: front three means the first three letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A racehorse falls near the front at Aintree.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse of the Grand National. A fell is a hill in northern England, and 'maybe' marks it as an example; 'fell' wants to be a horse falling.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern English, a fell is a hill or upland, an instance of a mountain.

clue.text: I was in charge of revolutionary food shop

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: led means was in charge

explanation.surface: A rebel boasts of having run a food shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling prepared foods.

clue.text: Sticky stuff covering poor Arnie's flower

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around another piece

parts.note: gum is sticky stuff

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gum is smeared over Arnie's sorry flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' shuffles ARNIE into ERANI; 'covering' puts GUM around it, split as G and UM. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The geranium is a common garden and pot plant grown for its bright blooms.

clue.text: Grand complex surrounds European area of cultivation

indicators.note: surrounds means one piece goes around another
complex means intricate, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand complex encloses a European plot of farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' shuffles GRAND into GARDN, which 'surrounds' places around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is a plot of ground where plants are grown and tended.

clue.text: Irregular money in South Africa doctor raised

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor in South Africa raised irregular amounts of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means without regular pattern or order, haphazard.

clue.text: Golf equipment also carried by gentleman working

indicators.note: carried by means held inside another piece

parts.note: sir is how a gentleman is addressed
and means also
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A working gentleman also carries his golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: A sand iron is an old name for a sand wedge, a club for bunker shots.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand iron is a golf club designed for playing out of bunkers.

clue.text: Supporter runs away from mass meeting

indicators.note: away from means the piece is taken out of the other

parts.note: a rally is a mass meeting
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A supporter flees from a crowded rally.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a backer or helper, one who supports a cause.

clue.text: Quote Italian in Church

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
It is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: Quote some Italian in church.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to quote a passage or author as evidence.

clue.text: Way of cooking meat in France, on vacation

definitions.note: flambé describes food cooked this way, an adjective standing for the method

indicators.note: in places the meat inside the emptied country
on vacation means emptied out, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: lamb is a meat

explanation.surface: How meat is cooked in France while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' means emptied, so France keeps only its first and last letters, and 'in' places the meat between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Flambé food is doused in spirit and set alight, a showy cooking technique.

clue.text: Soon perspire regularly in full-body garment

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: You will soon sweat in an all-in-one outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A onesie is a one-piece garment covering the torso and limbs, worn for lounging.
